title: Attention Theories: Broadbent's Filter, Attenuation, Late Selection, Multimode, Perceptual Load, Feature Integration
summary: Broadbent's filter theory (1958); attenuation theory (1962); Deutsch & Deutsch late selection; Johnston & Heinz multimode; Lavie's perceptual load; Treisman's feature integration theory.
objectives: Contrast early and late selection models.
revision: Attention theories: Broadbent = early filter; Attenuation = weakening not blocking; Late selection = all processed; Perceptual load = load determines distractor processing; Feature integration = two stages (preattentive + binding).
traps: Feature integration = two stages (preattentive + focused attention).
confusions: Believing attenuation completely blocks unattended messages.

notes.t: Broadbent proposed that a selective filter blocks unattended messages early in processing, before semantic analysis. Only attended information passes through.
Treisman's attenuation theory proposes that unattended messages are weakened (attenuated) rather than completely blocked. Low-threshold words (e.g., your name) can still get through.
Deutsch & Deutsch proposed that all messages are fully processed semantically, and selection occurs late, based on importance/meaning.
Johnston & Heinz proposed that selection can occur at multiple stages: early, intermediate, or late, depending on processing demands.
Lavie proposed that distractor processing depends on perceptual load: high load leaves no capacity for distractors; low load allows distractor processing.
Treisman proposed two stages: preattentive processing (automatic feature detection) and focused attention (binding features into objects).
UGC NET frequently asks to distinguish early (Broadbent) vs late (Deutsch & Deutsch) selection and to explain feature integration theory stages.

mnemonics.title: BATLMPF
mnemonics.text: B — Broadbent (early filter), A — Attenuation (weakening), T — Late selection (all processed), L — Lavie (perceptual load), M — Multimode (multiple stages), F — Feature integration (two stages)

flashcards.a: Early selection — blocks unattended messages before semantic analysis.
Two stages: preattentive detection + focused attention binding.

diagrams.caption: Broadbent's filter theory: sensory input → filter → detector → store
Feature integration theory: preattentive → focused attention binding
